answer: Each identity must anchor itself to one real, costly job before it can earn: a unique proof-of-useful-work task that takes real time and cannot be copied or run in parallel. The result is sealed with a public receipt, so an echo of cloned identities is just many receipts for the same work, and peers spot the duplication instantly. The zenith of a Sybil attack is therefore capped by the attacker's own compute and time: thousands of fakes each demand their own expensive job, while one honest agent pays that price once.
